 Tee K.O. 2 is the first game announced for The Jackbox Party Pack 10 , and is a sequel to Tee K.O. .The sequel to perennial shirt-combat favorite Tee K.O. – arriving to Tee Shirt Island to draw, write, and mash things together to create shirts that go head-to-head in thrilling, fabric-rending combat.

 In Tee K.O. 2 , the age of t-shirt tournaments is back under the eye of the tournament mistress. Unlike other sequels, this one has a modern twist where the combatants participating in this fatal feud of fabric and slogans are all beloved characters from other installments of The Jackbox Party Pack franchise.

 Innovation [ ] 

 A new cast of playable characters. (Jackbox Games posted them to their social mediums under the #TeeKO2uesday hashtag from May 16 to August 29.)

 Choose your champion. Once garments enter the battle area, you and the audience vote to determine the winner of each match-up… including a new Final Round that decides the grand champion of Tee Shirt Island.

 Call out the reinforcements. This time there will be new drawing tools in the game to create your perfect clothing warrior. You can also change the design to look better with a different font, you can also change it to a different item entirely, such as a hoodie.

 Gameplay [ ] 

 Players start off Round 1 by drawing graphics until the time runs out, then Round 2 features those same players needing to write slogans, Round 3 requires the players combine graphics with drawings, all while deciding the font and what type of garment it should be displayed on.

 Now players must fight in a Bracketeering -inspired showdown to see who will make it to the final round, where players will need to tap on their devices to make sure that the garment they've sided with overtakes the other and is deemed the soul victor of the tournament!

 Trivia [ ] 

 The masks from the game's reveal trailer have official templates you can follow to make your own.

 The fact that the only playable character from the original Tee K.O. is Gyokuto, and the appearance of other characters in the background as ghosts, implies that everyone from Tee K.O. died except for her.

 Mayonnaise and Stereo Robot's character artwork poses could be references to character art from Super Smash Brothers Ultimate and Super Smash Brothers for 3DS and Wii U respectively, with Mayonnaise's pose being similar to Wolf's artwork from Ultimate and Mega Man's artwork from 3DS and Wii U .

 Tee K.O. 2 is a party video game and one of five games featured in The Jackbox Party Pack 10 . It is the sequel to Tee K.O. 

 Gameplay

 At the beginning of the first round , players will be asked to draw three drawings on their device. On their device, they have a selection of tools to use for drawing, including a color palette with a pen for drawing, a marker for coloring in, an eraser, and a base color for their canvas.

 Unlike the first game, if a player finishes a drawing while the timer is still going, they will immediately move on to the next drawing.

 Once all players' drawings are submitted, they will move on to the slogan writing phase, where they must write at least 4 or more slogans and/or phrases as they can.

 After that, they will move on to the make a shirt phase, where players are given a set of random drawings and slogans to put on a shirt. There are also options to change the font of the slogan, as well as the type of garment players want to use, including a hoodie, tank top, or the default t-shirt. 

 Once everyone has made their shirt, each design will face off against each other in a bracket-style tournament, where the winner of each matchup is determined by the votes of the players and Audience (if the Audience is present).

 The second round plays out the same, except players will be asked to make one more drawing. Unlike the previous game, players are given the option to edit a drawing that was made in the previous round, or make an entirely new one. In the make a shirt phase, drawings and slogans made in round 1 and round 2 can be used.

 In the final round , there is no drawing, writing, or shirt making phases. Instead, the winning shirts from the two previous rounds will face off against each other in a button-mashing style competition. Players will vote for their favorite design, and continue to vote until the power meter of that shirt is completely filled.

 The dragon then burns the losing shirt, before transitioning to it wearing the winning shirt, effectively declaring the winner of the game.
